title: Response orchestration: Trace linklets & runbook stitcher
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: On-call teams currently open separate traces, dashboards, and docs during incidents. Attaching raw traces or full traces to PagerDuty and Slack threads increases noise and often contains PII. Goal: Provide a first-class incident enrichment pipeline that composes small, targeted 'trace linklets' (contextualized span excerpts + synthesized summary), stitches relevant runbook steps into the incident thread, and auto-seeds a postmortem skeleton when an incident is promoted. This ticket builds the orchestration glue: PD and Slack hooks, runbook template insertion logic, trace summarization pipeline, and safe artifact storage/links.
acceptance_criteria: PagerDuty incidents can be enriched via an API call that attaches a signed evaluation bundle URL and a 3-line synthesized trace summary
Slack incident threads receive a formatted runbook snippet with buttons: 'Acknowledge', 'Create Postmortem Draft', and 'Attach Trace Linklet'
Trace linklet generation runs within 4s for scoped 1-3 span excerpts and includes span metadata, annotated hypotheses, and a short natural language summary
Artifacts stored in secure object storage with 7-day default TTL and optional extended retention via config

A postmortem skeleton draft (template) is created in the internal docs system when a user clicks 'Create Postmortem Draft' and the draft contains incident timeline, attached linklets, and a starter hypothesis section
PII-scrubbing runs on any attached payloads and is configurable per-team; no raw logs or full traces are embedded in Slack or PD descriptions
tasks: Spec: finalize trace linklet schema and minimal span extraction rules (owner: Aisha)
API: implement PD enrichment endpoint with rate-limiting and HMAC auth (owner: Marco)
Slack: compose message builder + interactive buttons and modal to confirm postmortem draft creation (owner: Nikhil)
Storage: object storage adapter with signed short-lived URLs and TTL policy (owner: SRE team)
Summarization: lightweight summarizer chain for span excerpts (owner: Research/Applied ML)
Security: PII scrubber integration and audit logging for attachments (owner: Security)
E2E tests: simulate incident creation -> PD enrichment -> Slack flow -> postmortem draft creation (owner: QA)
Docs: runbook template + how-to for on-call (owner: Developer Experience)
Telemetry: metrics for enrichment latency, linklet generation errors, PD API success rate (owner: Observability)
Rollout: feature flag gating and canary to 10% of incidents before full enablement (owner: Product)
decision_log: 2026-02-19: Decided to use 'linklet' model (small artifact + summary) vs attaching full trace to avoid noise and privacy issues
2026-02-22: Agreed to store artifacts in object storage with signed URLs and 7-day default TTL; extended retention will be opt-in per team
2026-02-27: Chose HMAC-based PD webhook auth rather than PD-owned attachments due to cross-account permission friction
2026-03-03: Trade-off: summarize 3 spans max for 1st pass to keep generation <4s; future enhancement to extend via async retrieval
outstanding_risks: Risk: Summaries could omit crucial causal spans—mitigation: include span metadata links and a 'fetch full trace' button guarded by SSO
Risk: Abuse of artifact generation leading to S3 cost spikes—mitigation: soft quota per team + rate limits
Risk: Slack message size / interactive rate limits—mitigation: compress payloads and rely on signed URLs for attachment previews
integration_notes: PagerDuty: will use Events API v2 'payload' enrichment path and include signed_url in incident.notes; link will expire per TTL
Slack: use block kit with contextual 'Runbook' blocks and action_ids mapped to internal endpoints that verify user via OIDC
Runbooks: templates stored in Confluence; postmortem draft uses a Confluence REST API template endpoint (docs: https://confluence.internal.redwood/obs/postmortems)
GitHub PR: PR will live in repo redwood/ops-enrichment (prototype branch: eng/20734-runbook-stitcher)
Audit: every enrichment call logs event_id, user_id, team_id and checksum of attached linklet
notes: Initial spike implemented a PoC that generates a linklet for a 2-span error path; latency measured at ~3.5s including summarization (prototype branch at https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-enrichment/tree/eng-20734-poc)
Design feedback (2026-03-05): product requested an 'escalate to SRE' button in Slack that creates a PD incident and attaches linklets
Security review kickoff scheduled for 2026-03-10 with secops; checklist includes PII rules, signed URL entropy, and retention controls
tests_and_metrics: Unit tests for trace extraction and scrubber rules
Integration tests for PD + Slack end-to-end flow using recorded fixtures
SLO: enrichment endpoint P99 latency < 2s under normal load, linklet generation p99 < 6s
Dashboard: new 'Incident Enrichment' panel in Console showing enrichment rate, success/failure, avg linklet size, and cost estimate
